118.0.0.en: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: because his mercy endureth for ever.

118.0.1.en: The writer of the psalm, and this verse may have been said by the king or the high priest, calls upon everyone, without distinction, to praise and thank the Lord for two things:

118.0.2.en: 1- That the Lord is good, that is, He does good things and bestows many blessings on mankind, and at the same time He is perfect in His virtues, shining upon humanity with His light so that it may learn from Him.

118.0.3.en: 2- That His mercy is great and continues for ever. He is tender and forgives sins, and not only at a particular time but throughout our whole life on earth; and in eternity also His mercy continues in the form of His gifts and His great blessings, which we do not deserve.

118.1.0.en: Let Israel now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.

118.1.1.en: 1- The psalm calls Israel, who are the people of God, to contemplate the greatness of God and to praise Him for His goodness and His continuing mercy toward them. He did many good things for them: He fed them manna and gave them water to drink in the wilderness, and He gave them the land of Canaan, which flows with milk and honey. His mercy also continued with them: He rescued them from the bondage of Egypt, from the bondage in the age of the Judges, and likewise from the Assyrian captivity and the Babylonian captivity...

118.1.2.en: 2- In this verse the specification begins. It singles out Israel, the people of God, because the first verse was an invitation to the whole world; and it singles out Israel because they believe in God, so they know His goodness and mercy, and therefore it is natural that they should praise Him and thank Him.

118.2.0.en: Let the house of Aaron now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.

118.2.1.en: The specification in the praise increases, and it calls the house of Aaron, that is, the priests, because God singled them out with the blessing of the priesthood, and destroyed those who opposed them and murmured against them, namely Korah, Dathan, Abiram and those with them. He also granted them to draw near to Him in His service. And God proclaimed the greatness of the priesthood when Aaron's rod budded.

118.3.0.en: Let them now that fear the LORD say, that his mercy endureth for ever.

118.3.1.en: 1- The fourth group that the psalm calls to praise God is those who fear the Lord, that is, those who revere Him. By this it means the believers among His people who fear Him, and also those among the Gentiles who fear Him and will join His people and believe. These feel the goodness of God and His favors more than others do, and also His mercy that lasts for ever.

118.3.2.en: 2- It called four groups to praise in the four verses, and these signify the four corners of the world, that is, a prophecy about Christianity, which spreads throughout the whole world. The believers praise God from the four corners of the world.

118.3.3.en: 3- In the verses (vv. 2-4) it begins with the word "let ... say", whether for Israel, or the house of Aaron, or those who fear the Lord; that is, they declare praise and thanksgiving to God so as to move the hearts of those around them, that they may join them in the praise.

118.3.4.en: Praising God and thanking Him makes you feel God's love for you, and it gladdens the heart of God, so His gifts and blessings to you increase, and joy spreads in the hearts of those around you. May you not forget praise every day, even if only with a small part of the Midnight Praise, or one psalm of praise.

118.4.s.en: (2) Trusting in the Lord the Savior

118.4.0.en: I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.

118.4.2.en: 1- David, or every person in distress, or Christ in the midst of His sufferings as a representative of mankind, cries out and asks God to bring him out of his distress. And because God is unlimited, that is, He has all spaciousness, He is able to loosen my distress and make room for me, so that I do not feel the distress though it is present; He grants me peace and strength and gives me rest, so I walk with success and vigor.

118.4.3.en: 2- When the sufferer calls on God while in the midst of afflictions, God hears him and gives him peace, and then promises him complete rest and release, and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him in eternity, where there is complete spaciousness.

118.4.4.en: 3- If I am suffering in my distress, I cannot ask a human being, because he is limited like me and lives in the midst of the afflictions of the world. But the only One who has all spaciousness is God, because He is unlimited, and therefore He alone is able to give me rest in the midst of the affliction, as the holy Fathers said: "Do not place your hope in a human being, but in God."

118.5.0.en: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?

118.5.1.en: When the sufferer feels that the Lord is on his side, that is, he has gained by faith the perfect God in His spaciousness, he no longer fears any human being, meaning that no human being can trouble him, because he has gained peace and rest within himself. Even if he suffers in the body, he is in inner peace and fears no man. David was pursued by Saul for many years and was not disturbed, because God was with him.

118.6.0.en: The LORD is with me among my helpers, and I shall look upon my enemies.

118.6.1.en: If I have any resources, such as money, health or relationships, I thank God for them because He gave them to me, but I hold fast to God my helper and boast in Him, for He is my true support, and He is able to use whatever resources He has given me. In this way I see the weakness of my enemies, the demons, whom God will drive away from me and give me victory over them.

118.7.0.en: It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in man. It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in princes.

118.7.1.en: 1- Here the psalm states an important truth: that reliance and refuge are in God alone, and not in any human being, because God alone is able to do all things, while human beings are weak.

118.7.2.en: 2- Even if human beings are rulers, they are also weak and cannot be relied upon. Despite King Artaxerxes' support for Nehemiah, this did not prevent Tobiah, Sanballat and Geshem from opposing him. And despite King Darius' friendship with Daniel, this did not prevent the princes of the kingdom from rising against the king and threatening him with death, and taking Daniel and casting him into the lions' den for six days; but God preserved him and sent him food by the hand of the prophet Habakkuk (Dan 14:36).

118.8.0.en: All nations compassed me about: but in the name of the LORD will I destroy them. They compassed me about; yea, they compassed me about: but in the name of the LORD I will destroy them. They compassed me about like bees; they are quenched as the fire of thorns: for in the name of the LORD I will destroy them. Compassed me: surrounded me closely and clung to me.

118.8.1.en: 1- David, or Christ, or every suffering believer declares that the wicked and unbelievers surround him and try to harm him, come very near to him, besiege him and even kill him. He likens them to bees around the honeycomb, that is, their numbers are great and they are able to strike and sting the one they surround. He likens them also to a fire blazing in thorns, which spreads quickly through them; but by the power of God he is able to overcome them and destroy them.

118.8.2.en: 2- The believer's reliance on the name of the Lord protects him and takes vengeance on his enemies, the demons. And he repeats the name of the Lord three times, after the likeness of the Holy Trinity.

118.9.0.en: Thou hast thrust sore at me that I might fall: but the LORD helped me.

118.9.1.en: Thrust sore at me: pushed me forcefully so that I would fall.

118.9.3.en: Though the afflictions were very severe and pushed me to fall, the Lord supported me with power, so the demons did not prevail. So I do not fear the force of the wars as long as God is with me, protecting me from any blow of the enemy. And I am not disturbed if the affliction increases upon me, for in the end God must intervene as long as I have taken refuge in Him. And if God permits afflictions, He gives peace during them, so that a person may benefit from them.

118.10.0.en: The LORD is my strength and song, and is become my salvation.

118.10.1.en: 1- When I see the wonderful work of God within afflictions, and His power, I sing and praise His holy name, because He always saves me from every affliction.

118.10.2.en: 2- Because of the greatness of this verse, we find that it is taken from the song of Moses (Ex 15:2) and was repeated by Isaiah (Isa 12:2), and the Church repeats it on Great Friday in the hymn "Thine is the power and the glory."

118.10.3.en: 3- "Is become my salvation" speaks of the salvation of Christ, which He accomplished by the Cross, and I obtain it by faith through the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace.

118.11.0.en: The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tabernacles of the righteous: the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. The right hand of the LORD is exalted: the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly.

118.11.2.en: 1- From the dwellings of the righteous and the just there rise hymns and praises to God their Savior. The tabernacles refer to the booths in which they used to dwell during the Feast of Tabernacles, at which this psalm is recited. This singing continues throughout their lives, and grows stronger in the eternal life.

118.11.3.en: 2- The right hand of the Lord refers to His power, which appeared in His Incarnation in the fullness of time. For it speaks of the right hand, which represents the body, and it is mentioned three times to signify the Holy Trinity. And this power of God is exalted above all the powers of the demons who fight me, and of the wicked who follow them.

118.12.0.en: I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD.

118.12.1.en: Though I meet severe afflictions that almost cost me my life by their harshness, God rescues me with great power, so I live with Him during the afflictions and come out of them, and I even speak of the wonders of God with me, so I preach to all who are distressed and strengthen the righteous in the faith. This is what happened with David, whom Saul pursued and often tried to kill, yet he reigned over the children of Israel and was the greatest of its kings. And Christ suffered to the point of death, and then rose from the dead. And this is repeated with every believer who holds fast to God, so he comes out of afflictions with abundant blessings, and tells of the works of God with him.

118.13.0.en: The LORD hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.

118.13.1.en: The afflictions that come upon me, even if they are harsh, are chastenings from God my Father who loves me, and He uses these chastenings to save me from my weaknesses and my sins. And I also choose fellowship with Him during the affliction, so I live and the death of sin does not overcome me, but I enjoy the life of righteousness.

118.13.2.en: Do not be disturbed by the multitude of afflictions, for they are your way to the Kingdom. Even if they are many, you will experience in them abundant blessings that you cannot taste outside of afflictions, and your heart will rejoice more than all those around you.

118.14.s.en: (3) Worship is thanksgiving to the Savior

118.14.0.en: Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the LORD: This gate of the LORD, into which the righteous shall enter. I will praise thee: for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.

118.14.1.en: 1- The gates of righteousness are the gates of the Temple through which the believer wants to enter in order to offer his worship to God, and when he is permitted to enter he praises God and thanks Him. In the New Testament they are the gates of the Church into which he enters, and he receives the greatest gift from God, which is His Body and Blood and all the sacraments of the Church, and he enjoys prayer in the presence of God, so he praises Him and glorifies Him.

118.14.2.en: 2- The one who asks for the gates of righteousness to be opened is Christ, whose spirit ascends after His death to enter Paradise and the Kingdom, after He completed the redemption of mankind, proclaiming the possibility of man's return to heaven, as stated in (Ps 24:7, 9). And He praises the Lord on behalf of all mankind; that is, mankind thanks God who restored to it the grace of entering heaven after the redemption of Christ.

118.14.3.en: 3- Those who enter the Temple and the Church are the righteous, that is, the just, who are the believers who want to live with God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

118.14.4.en: 4- The one who calls for the gates of righteousness to be opened is God, who wants to enter the hearts of His children who believe in Him and love righteousness. Then His children rejoice and thank Him for His humility in dwelling within them, and because He answered their requests in (v. 19), opened to them the gates of righteousness and virtue, and gave them strength by dwelling in them, that they may enjoy all that He accomplished on the Cross for their sake.

118.14.5.en: 5- In ancient times they used to walk in procession to the Temple at the Feast of Passover and the Feast of Tabernacles, and when they reached the gates of the Temple they would call out with (v. 19), and the one in charge of the gates would answer them from inside with (v. 20), and then they would go on repeating the following verses of the psalm.

118.14.6.en: 6- The gate of the Lord is Baptism, through which the righteous, the children of God, enter the Church after their baptism.

118.14.7.en: 7- The stone which the builders refused is perhaps the one to which Daniel referred as the stone cut out without hands which became a great mountain (Dan 2:43), and what is meant by it, of course, is Christ, born of the Virgin without the seed of man, and who became a great salvation for all mankind.

118.15.0.en: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvellous in our eyes.

118.15.1.en: 1- When the Jews were building the Temple of Solomon they found a large stone that had been cut, and they saw that it was larger than the other stones and did not fit with them, so they left it aside. After building the two walls that met at right angles they found a gap in the corner that nothing could fill but this rejected stone, and they marvelled that this stone became the most important of the stones, for it became the head of the corner, and the two walls rest on it and are made firm.

118.15.2.en: And this became a proverb among the Jews, "that the stone which the builders rejected became the head of the corner", until they learned that this was a symbol of Christ.

118.15.3.en: 2- Christ referred to (v. 22) in (Mt 21:42) when speaking with the Jews, and declared that this stone was a type of Him. The priests, the scribes and the Pharisees rejected Him, opposed Him and crucified Him, but the believers afterward discovered that He is the Redeemer and Savior, the One risen from the dead, so this became marvellous in their eyes.

118.15.4.en: 3- These two verses apply to all the saints of the Old and New Testaments. The prophets were opposed by the Jews, such as Moses and Elijah, Isaiah and Jeremiah, and some of them were killed, sawn asunder with a saw like Isaiah, or stoned with stones like Jeremiah; but the believers afterward discovered that their words were the word of God, and that it was fulfilled and realized in their lives, so it became marvellous in their eyes. The same was repeated with the Apostles, such as Peter and Paul, who endured many sufferings and were martyred, though their words were the word of life.

118.15.5.en: Likewise the lives of the martyrs, with whose blood the Church was watered, so it grew and flourished and became strong over the generations. And this remains marvellous in the eyes of all until now.

118.15.6.en: Do not reject the word of God that you hear, and do not neglect it lest you be condemned by it. Try to carry it out as much as you can, even if only partially. God rejoices in your attempt and supports you. Persevere in your spiritual striving, and be confident that you will triumph in the end.

118.16.s.en: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

118.16.0.en: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it. Save now, I beseech thee, O LORD: O LORD, I beseech thee, send now prosperity. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD: we have blessed you out of the house of the LORD. God is the LORD, which hath shewed us light: bind the sacrifice with cords, even unto the horns of the altar.

118.16.1.en: 1- The day is the day of the Resurrection, on which the completion of salvation was declared for mankind, for everyone who believes in Him, and the Church celebrates it not only at the Feast of the Resurrection and the fifty days that follow, but also on every Sunday. And this day, the day of the Resurrection, is also meant to include everything connected with redemption: the Incarnation of Christ, His preaching, His entry into Jerusalem, and His death on the Cross.

118.16.2.en: 2- The believers rejoice in this day, the day of salvation, and ask God to grant them this salvation by saying "Save now, O LORD; O LORD, send now prosperity", that is, to save them from their sins and rescue them from the authority of the devil.

118.16.3.en: 3- These four verses apply clearly to Christ, for the Jews received Christ in Jerusalem with the words of (v. 26), proclaiming that He is the Savior who comes for their salvation in the name of the Lord.

118.16.4.en: 4- The people coming in procession to the Temple say the verses (vv. 24-26), and the Levites answer them from inside with the words of (v. 27), meaning that God is the light of our life, and he asks the people to arrange themselves and enter in procession to the altar, to celebrate and rejoice in this great feast, the Feast of Passover or the Feast of Tabernacles. As for the Church of the New Testament, what is meant is that the Lord Jesus Christ is God, and He has enlightened and shone upon us by His salvation which He accomplished on the Cross, and He asks the believers to come to the altar of the New Testament in a great and joyful procession, to partake of the Holy Mysteries.

118.16.5.en: This is the greatest celebration of the Church.

118.16.6.en: 5- Perhaps the prophet David said these verses when he had completed his victories, and rejoiced, and kept a feast to God, and entered His Temple, and offered thanksgiving sacrifices to Him.

118.17.0.en: Thou art my God, and I will praise thee: thou art my God, I will exalt thee. O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

118.17.1.en: 1- The psalm ends with thanking God, praising Him and magnifying Him for His goodness and also for all His works that the psalm mentioned.

118.17.2.en: 2- The last verse of this psalm is the beginning of the psalm, so the psalm begins and ends with praise. And verse 28 was proclaimed by the king, and (v. 29) was sung by the choir of the Levites.

118.17.3.en: 3- Perhaps David wrote these verses in the spirit of prophecy, for he saw Christ his God, and thanked Him for the salvation that He would offer on behalf of all mankind.

118.17.4.en: Do not forget to thank God after every work that He does with you or through you, so your love for God increases, your confidence in yourself grows, and new blessings from God overflow upon you.

118.17.5.en: The word of God: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD" (v. 1). Introduction:

118.17.6.en: 1- Its writer: This psalm has no title, so it is one of the orphan psalms, but most of the Fathers and the elders of the Jews incline to attribute it to David.

118.17.8.en: a- David wrote it after he was anointed king by the hand of Samuel and before he ascended the throne, that is, in the period when he was fleeing from the face of Saul, and he was in his early twenties at that time.

118.17.9.en: b- Some of the Fathers consider that David wrote it over the course of his life as his private memoirs of his fellowship with God and his enjoyment of His word. And he collected them at the end of his life, and they became this psalm.

118.17.10.en: 3- The purpose of this psalm is to speak of the greatness of the word of God, its power, and its effect in the lives of believers. Praying with this psalm moves the one who prays it to love the word of God, to care for it, and even to apply it in his life.

118.17.11.en: 4- This psalm consists of twenty-two sections, each section beginning with one of the Hebrew letters of the alphabet, which number twenty-two letters. And each section of this psalm is made up of eight verses, each verse in it beginning with the same letter in the Hebrew language.

118.17.12.en: 5- The word of God, or its synonyms, is mentioned in all the verses of this psalm, which number 176 verses, except for only two verses, which are (vv. 122, 132).

118.17.13.en: 6- The word of God and its synonyms mentioned in this psalm are ten, which are:

118.17.19.en: 7- The words of this psalm show that its writer is a spiritual man who loves the word of God and prayer, and lives by the word of God in his life, and he is a young man who was accustomed to repeating the word of God and suffering in it. This is what David did while tending sheep, and after he was anointed king he continued to repeat the word of God and meditate on it, and even in his afflictions, when he fled from Saul who pursued him from place to place to kill him, he remained holding fast to the word of God.

118.17.20.en: 8- There is a similarity between this psalm and the Book of Deuteronomy, for the purpose of both is the word of God, His commandments and His law.

118.17.21.en: 9- Many of the Fathers consider that the Book of Psalms is the heart of the Old Testament, and the heart of the Book of Psalms is this psalm.

118.17.22.en: 10- This psalm suits the one who prays it in all the circumstances of his life, whether in affliction or in ease, in youth and in old age. And it suits all the hours of the day, whether in the early morning, or throughout the day, or at night, or at midnight, or at the times of the dawn hours. It is a psalm for all the hours of the day and all the days of life.

118.17.23.en: 11- This psalm helps everyone who wants to learn meditation (lahaj), or murmuring (hadhidh), that is, repeating the word of God in order to enjoy fellowship with Him, since by repeating the word of God he draws near to God Himself, so he loves Him and lives for Him, and experiences new depths of God's work in his life.

118.17.24.en: 12- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms, because the awaited Messiah is the Word of God, Christ our God (Jn 1:1). In addition, the number 8, of which each part of the psalm is composed, signifies eternity, that is, Christ the Word of God who reigns in eternity with His children who believe in Him, that they may praise Him continually.

118.17.25.en: 13- This psalm includes many meanings and aspects of the word of God, the most important of which are:

118.17.26.en: a - A source of spiritual comfort in the midst of sufferings.

118.17.27.en: b - It encourages praise and thanksgiving.

118.17.28.en: c - It satisfies the soul and enriches it.

118.17.29.en: d - It guides and directs a person in his life on earth, especially in afflictions.

118.17.30.en: e - It gives spiritual enlightenment to the one who meditates on it.

118.17.31.en: f - It gives life and a sense of God.

118.17.32.en: g - It supports a person in his spiritual striving throughout his life.

118.17.33.en: h - It shows God's reward for those who hold fast to His commandments, and so encourages them to persevere in the striving.

118.17.34.en: i - It nourishes prayer of the heart and moves a person to constant prayer.

118.17.35.en: j - It is Christ, the unlimited God; because the commandment is exceedingly wide, beyond all imagination.

118.17.36.en: 14- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the Midnight prayer in the First Service, to make the one who prays live by the word of God; then it prepares us for the life of repentance in the Second Service, and after this it gives us preparation for eternity in the Third Service.

118.17.37.en: The first section (Aleph): the blessings of keeping the commandment (vv. 1-8). The aim:

118.17.38.en: The psalm pronounces blessed the one who keeps the commandment with all his heart, because he receives the blessing of keeping away from sin, and likewise obtains forgiveness if he sins. And he thanks God for His gifts, and so rejoices, until he reaches his goal, which is blessed eternity.
